newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt shortlists advisers for Airports Co.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt shortlists advisers for Airports Co.

text.p: The South African government said on Thursday it had shortlisted three groups to advise it on the restructuring of state-owned Airports Company.
- SBC Warburg in partnership with Gobodo Inc, a firm of accountants and consultants
- Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank in partnership with Morgan Stanley and Coordinated Management Consulting

Transport Minister Mac Maharaj and Public Enterprises Minister Stella Sigcau said in a joint statement that the three parties had been invited for interviews with the restructuring committee on July 25 and an announcement on the successful candidate would be made shortly after.
A total of 17 groups submitted bids for the position of adviser.
The government has previously indicated that it favours the initial part privatisation of the company, which operates South Africa's major aiports.
A minority strategic equity partner could be found in late 1997 or early 1998.
At least nine foreign firms have expressed interest in taking a stake in the company, which analysts estimate could be valued at around 2.5 billion rand.
